lead: The puerperium runs from delivery of the placenta until the genital organs return to the non-pregnant state: about 6 weeks (42 days). Immediate = first 24 h · early = to day 7 · remote = to 6 wk. Main dangers: sepsis, haemorrhage, VTE, mood disorders.
f: Physiological changes: the genital tract

Fundus at the umbilicus after birth, falls about 1 cm a day, not palpable by day 14 (still felt = subinvolution) · Uterus 1000 g → 60–100 g at 6 wk · Contraction closes the vessels ("living ligatures"); muscle shrinks by autolysis · New endometrium from the basal layer by day 10; placental site heals by 6 wk without a scar · Cervix 1 finger by day 10–14; os stays a transverse slit

sc: Day 7 after a normal delivery → Fundus midway between umbilicus and pubis

f: Lochia

Rubra day 1–4: red · Serosa day 5–9: pink-brown · Alba day 10 to 3–6 wk: yellow-white · Total about 250 mL; mild smell, never foul · Foul: infection · Red again or persistent rubra: retained tissue, subinvolution · None + fever: lochiometra

sc: Red lochia again at day 12, bulky uterus → Retained tissue

f: Physiological changes: other systems

Cardiac output rises straight after birth (autotransfusion): heart disease decompensates now · WBC up to 20–25 × 10⁹/L in the first days is normal · Hypercoagulable for 6 wk (VTE) · Diuresis day 2–5; void within 6 h (retention) · ≥ 38 °C is never normal · Blues in up to 80% on day 3–5

sc: Day 2, WBC 18 × 10⁹/L, afebrile and well → Reassure: normal leucocytosis

f: Return of ovulation
Not breastfeeding: ovulation from day 25, menses at 6–8 wk; start contraception by day 21 · Breastfeeding: prolactin blocks GnRH; but ovulation comes before the first period
Lactation

Prolactin makes milk · oxytocin: let-down and after-pains · Progesterone fall lets milk come in (day 3–4) · Colostrum to day 3: IgA, protein, laxative · Mature milk from 2 wk, about 750–800 mL/day · Cabergoline stops lactation
Postnatal care
Stay ≥ 24 h after a vaginal birth · Visits: 48–72 h, day 7–14, 6 wk (at least 4 contacts, WHO) · Check: vital signs, uterus and lochia, perineum or wound, breasts, bladder, legs, mood, baby

sc: Pad soaked hourly on day 9 → Secondary PPH

f: Investigations and treatments

Iron + folate for 3 months · Anti-D 500 IU IM within 72 h: RhD-negative, not sensitised, baby RhD-positive (+ Kleihauer) · Rubella non-immune: MMR before discharge; avoid pregnancy 1 month; breastfeeding fine · GDM: glucose test at 6 wk
Breastfeeding

Start within 1 hour, skin to skin · Exclusive for 6 months, on demand, 8–12 feeds a day · Continue to 2 years · Good attachment: mouth wide, chin on the breast, lower lip out · Benefits: fewer infections, less PPH, LAM, less breast and ovarian cancer
Contraindications to breastfeeding

Galactosaemia (absolute) · Untreated active TB: treat, express, isoniazid to the baby · HIV: exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months on ART, no mixed feeding · Drugs: cytotoxics, radioactive iodine, lithium, amiodarone, ergots, tetracycline, chloramphenicol · Not contraindications: hepatitis B (vaccine + HBIG), mastitis, caesarean

tr: Mastitis is not a reason to stop: keep feeding from that breast

f: Stopping lactation
After stillbirth or neonatal death: supportive bra, cold packs, no expressing · Cabergoline 1 mg once within 24 h · Avoid in pre-eclampsia or hypertension · Bromocriptine no longer used
Breastfeeding problems

Engorgement day 3–5, both breasts: feed often, express · Cracked nipples: correct the latch · Mastitis: red wedge, fever, week 2–3, S. aureus: keep feeding, flucloxacillin 500 mg 6-hourly × 10–14 d · Breast abscess: fluctuant mass: ultrasound, aspiration or I&D
Postnatal contraception

LAM: no period + full breastfeeding + baby under 6 months → 98% · Progestogen methods (POP, implant, DMPA, LNG-IUS): first choice while breastfeeding · COC: from day 21 if not breastfeeding; after 6 months if breastfeeding · IUD: within 48 h or after 4 wk · Tubal ligation: at CS or within 7 days, else after 6 wk

sc: Breastfeeding mother at 6 wk asks for the combined pill → Avoid until 6 months; POP, implant or IUD
LAM user, baby 4 months, starts solids → Start another method
